import type { Style } from '../types'

// Output tokens cost five times input on every Claude model, so the cheapest token is the one never written.
// One short section, added once at the end of the system prompt: it stays inside the prompt cache.

const ECONOMY = `# Output economy
Every token you write is paid for. Write the least text that fully answers.
- Start with the answer, command or change. No preamble ("Great question", "Let me…", "I'll…").
- No recap of what you just did beyond one line naming the result. No closing offers ("Let me know…", "Hope this helps").
- Do not restate the request, narrate routine tool calls, or echo back code and diffs the user can already see.
- Prefer a short list or a code block to paragraphs. Show at most 5 items per list; group and rank the rest.
- Batch related shell commands into one call. Read the part of a file you need (grep, sed -n, offsets), not the whole file, unless you are about to edit it.
- Brevity never deletes the answer: when asked to explain or walk through something, explain fully. Confirm before destructive actions as always.`

// Adapted from i-have-adhd by Ayoub Ghriss (github.com/ayghri/i-have-adhd, MIT).
const ADHD = `# ADHD-friendly output
The reader has ADHD: working memory is small, starting is the hardest step, and buried wins do not register. Shape every answer so it can be acted on now.
1. The first line is the next action: a command, a path, an edit. Context after it, if at all.
2. Multi-step work is a numbered list: one bounded action per step, the fewest steps that work.
3. If anything is left open, end with exactly one concrete next step doable in under two minutes.
4. No tangents: finish this, then offer a second issue as one separate question.
5. Restate where the work stands each turn ("Step 3 of 5 done: schema updated. Next: backfill.").
6. Time estimates in minutes or hours, never "a bit".
7. Make finished work visible: what now works and how to try it.
8. Errors are matter-of-fact: cause, location, fix. Never "Uh oh".
9. Show at most 5 items per list; group and rank the rest.
10. No preamble, no recap, no closing pleasantries.
Break these rules to explain fully when asked (with headers), to confirm before destructive actions, after three "still broken" turns (name the assumption that may be wrong, ask one diagnostic question), and to ask one short question when the request is genuinely ambiguous.
Batch related shell commands into one call, and read the part of a file you need rather than all of it.`

export const STYLE: Record<Style, string | undefined> = { off: undefined, terse: ECONOMY, adhd: ADHD }

export function isStyle(value: unknown): value is Style {
  return value === 'off' || value === 'terse' || value === 'adhd'
}

{
  "name": "model-router",
  "version": "1.2.0",
  "description": "Cache-aware model routing for Claude Code: each prompt goes to Haiku, Sonnet or Opus by what it needs, and a cheaper model only when that pays after the prompt-cache re-write. Crew mode adds warm per-model workers. Bash output is compressed rtk-style and answers drop the filler.",
  "author": {
    "name": "preisnerai"
  },
  "homepage": "https://github.com/preisnerai/claude-mods/tree/main/model-router",
  "repository": "https://github.com/preisnerai/claude-mods",
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": [
    "model-routing",
    "token-saving",
    "cost",
    "haiku",
    "sonnet",
    "opus",
    "prompt-cache",
    "rtk",
    "adhd"
  ],
  "types": "./types/index.d.ts",
  "userConfig": {
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mode",
      "description": "route moves the main session to another model when a prompt needs it and the cache math says it pays. crew keeps the main session on one orchestrator model from the first prompt on (its cache is never thrown away) and hands work of several tool calls to long-lived Haiku, Sonnet and Opus workers, each with its own warm cache.",
      "options": [
        "route",
        "crew"
      ],
      "default": "route"
    },
    "orchestrator": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Crew orchestrator",
      "description": "The model the main session stays on in crew mode.",
      "options": [
        "haiku",
        "sonnet",
        "opus"
      ],
      "default": "sonnet"
    },
    "escalate": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Harder tasks",
      "description": "auto moves a session to a stronger model when a prompt needs it (or tools keep failing); suggest only names it in the status line.",
      "options": [
        "auto",
        "suggest"
      ],
      "default": "auto"
    },
    "style": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Answer style",
      "description": "terse cuts preamble, recaps and closers; adhd also leads with the next action and numbers steps (after i-have-adhd); off leaves answers alone.",
      "options": [
        "terse",
        "adhd",
        "off"
      ],
      "default": "terse"
    },
    "compress": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Compress Bash output",
      "description": "Strips progress bars and passing tests, folds exact repeats, keeps every error line; file contents, diffs and data pass untouched. The last 200 compressed outputs stay whole in ~/.claude/model-router/tee.",
      "default": true
    },
    "useRtk": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Use rtk when installed",
      "description": "Hands plain cargo test, pytest, tsc, mypy and go build output to `rtk pipe` when the rtk binary is on PATH; a summary that drops the failures is refused.",
      "default": true
    },
    "cacheTtl": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Prompt cache lifetime",
      "description": "1h: Claude Code's default (writes cost 2x input, entries live an hour). 5m: for setups that write 5-minute entries (1.25x). The router's switch math uses it.",
      "options": [
        "1h",
        "5m"
      ],
      "default": "1h"
    },
    "judge": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Judge for unclear prompts",
      "description": "haiku asks claude-haiku-5-5 (about $0.0001) when the local rules can't tell. off: no judge; unclear prompts go to laya-serve when layaUrl is set, and otherwise keep the current model.",
      "options": [
        "haiku",
        "off"
      ],
      "default": "haiku"
    },
    "enableFable": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Route research to Fable",
      "description": "Lets proofs, new theories and bounds go to claude-fable-5-1. Turn on only if your plan includes Fable.",
      "default": false
    },
    "showNote": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Note beneath answers",
      "description": "A line under each answer naming the model and why, for surfaces with no status line.",
      "default": true
    },
    "layaUrl": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "laya-serve URL (optional)",
      "description": "A running laya-serve (e.g. http://localhost:8000) classifies unclear prompts on your machine for zero tokens, before the Haiku judge.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "layaApiKey": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "laya-serve API key",
      "description": "Sent as a Bearer token; leave empty when laya-serve runs without LAYA_API_KEY.",
      "sensitive": true,
      "default": ""
    },
    "haikuEffort": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Haiku effort",
      "description": "Effort when the router moves you to Haiku (on your own model your /effort stays, so its cache stays too).",
      "options": [
        "low",
        "medium",
        "high",
        "xhigh",
        "max"
      ],
      "default": "low"
    },
    "sonnetEffort": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sonnet effort",
      "description": "Effort when the router moves you to Sonnet (on your own model your /effort stays, so its cache stays too).",
      "options": [
        "low",
        "medium",
        "high",
        "xhigh",
        "max"
      ],
      "default": "medium"
    },
    "opusEffort": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Opus effort",
      "description": "Effort when the router moves you to Opus (on your own model your /effort stays, so its cache stays too).",
      "options": [
        "low",
        "medium",
        "high",
        "xhigh",
        "max"
      ],
      "default": "high"
    },
    "fableEffort": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Fable effort",
      "description": "Effort when the router moves you to Fable (on your own model your /effort stays, so its cache stays too).",
      "options": [
        "low",
        "medium",
        "high",
        "xhigh",
        "max"
      ],
      "default": "xhigh"
    }
  }
}
